dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Read main.rs, types.rs, decode.rs, runtime.rs AND spec.rs — the complete skeleton including the frozen public-contract files it must not modify, establishing the Value/stack model and decode wiring before editing.
Read run_tests.py and the spec-test harness format, ran an i32 baseline, and counted command types across all tests — orienting to the test surface and opcode families before implementing.

Task breakdown names specific stubbed/buggy targets (v128_get/set helpers, exec_one call wiring, validate_module), showing it identified which MVP functions were unimplemented vs present rather than guessing an interface.

When br.json and store-lane families misbehaved, it inspected br.0.wasm sections and dumped raw bytes to disambiguate encoding — sustained, targeted re-research against actual binary, matching the top-anchor probing behavior.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read every key source including the frozen spec.rs/main.rs, understood the value/stack model and 0xFD-style decode path, learned the spec-test format, and enumerated the opcode surface — clearing the level-5 bar comfortably. It went further to an explicit map of stubbed/buggy functions and integration points (level 8), and showed some level-10 behavior by probing specific wasm binaries byte-by-byte when families behaved unexpectedly. It stops short of a clear 10 because the compressed log shows no explicit spec-semantic pinning (saturation/NaN/lane-order) research; hence 8.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: Task decomposition: MVP work is split into sensible sub-tasks (v128 helpers, numeric ops, function calls, validate_module) and explicitly sequenced before SIMD, but SIMD itself is collapsed into just two tasks — 'Add SIMD opcode decoding' and 'Implement all SIMD ops in runtime' — with no per-family breakdown and no per-family spec_json done-checks.
Orientation before planning (reading skeleton, test runner, counting command types) — informs the decomposition but shows the plan was built on an understanding of the test surface, not random.
Decode-before-execute split for SIMD shows minimal dependency awareness, but the ~15 instruction families are never enumerated as ordered milestones.

SIMD verification happens as ad-hoc per-test debugging (store8_lane, br, etc.) after one big build, not as pre-planned family milestones each tied to its spec_json — confirming SIMD was treated as one undifferentiated push at the plan level.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent cleanly sequenced MVP before SIMD and gave the MVP half real sub-structure (component-level tasks in a rough dependency order), which lifts it above the bare 'vague two-phase idea' anchor (3). However, the SIMD half — the core of this dimension's ~15-family concern — was lumped into a single 'implement all SIMD ops' task with no family-level grouping and no per-family spec_json exit checks, so it falls short of the level-5 'groups SIMD into families, implementing family by family with matching spec test as checkpoint.' This places observed behavior between the anchors, at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: Establishes per-family baseline by running i32.json, inspects its structure, and writes a score.sh harness before broad implementation — deliberate fine-grained verification setup.

Sustained implement→run→categorize-FAIL→fix→recheck loop across MVP families (i32, br_table, conversions/f32, malformed globals, assert_invalid), localizing failures by category rather than reading only a pass rate.
Drills into specific failing assertions: inspects br.0.wasm sections, dumps bytes at line 995, checks simd_store8_lane — distinguishing encoding mismatches from semantic bugs.
Runs the full aggregate runner repeatedly after each fix and re-examines MVP files post-SIMD, treating the aggregate as a monitored signal toward 1.0 rather than a one-shot final check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs the correct systematic loop of the 8 anchor: per-family json after implementing MVP features, reads specific FAIL categories, fixes, re-runs to green, and periodically runs the full runner while re-guarding MVP files against SIMD regressions. It exceeds the 5 anchor with byte-level diagnosis distinguishing encoding from semantic causes and continuous aggregate monitoring, but falls short of 10 because SIMD families were verified mostly via the full runner rather than isolated per-family jsons and no explicit NaN/saturation/lane-order semantic reasoning is visible.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: Created a 7-item task ledger spanning the major work families (v128 helpers, numeric ops, calls, validate_module, SIMD decode, SIMD ops, MVP iteration), establishing a maintained checklist of what must be done.
TaskUpdate → completed at multiple points across the run, showing the ledger was kept current as families finished rather than being abandoned mid-way.
Repeated per-family failure categorization (i32, br_table, conversions/f32, invalid/malformed) — actively tracking which families still have failing assertions.
Repeated full-suite rescoring interleaved with fixes, reconciling the aggregate score against ongoing work.
Drilled into a single stuck SIMD assertion (store8_lane, dumping bytes at line 995), indicating awareness of being stuck on one case rather than thrashing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a family-level task ledger and kept it updated as families completed (above the level-5 anchor of a static checklist), and went further by repeatedly categorizing failures per family and reconciling them against repeated aggregate rescoring, plus isolating a single stuck assertion — behaviors characteristic of the level-8 anchor. However, the checklist was coarse (family- not opcode-granular), and there is no observable quantification of the gap to 1.0, effort reallocation to highest-remaining families, or catching cross-family regressions, keeping it short of 8. This places observed behavior at a 6, interpolating between the 5 and 8 anchors. Confidence is medium because the log contains only actions, not the agent's prose or tool observations.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Repeated 'Categorize failures' steps (i32 failures, non-invalid failures, conversions, assert_invalid text messages) interleaved with targeted edits — the agent steps back to group stubborn failures by family and reconsiders the relevant handling rather than patching each assertion blindly.

Inspects malformed global cases, then makes three decode.rs edits — investigating the decoding assumption at the source before adjusting, consistent with reconsidering an assumption when a family fails.
'Inspect line 995' then 'Dump bytes' then Edit — root-cause byte-level investigation of a specific decoding failure before fixing, rather than surface patching.

Edits touch types.rs and decode.rs (representation/decoding layers), showing willingness to adjust beyond a single file, but no observable evidence of a decisive one-shot structural refactor that flips many assertions together.

dimensions.reasoning: The observable action pattern shows a consistent diagnose-by-family and inspect-bytes-before-editing rhythm: the agent categorizes stubborn failures and investigates root causes at the decode/representation layer before adjusting, which matches the level-5 anchor (steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption when a family fails). There is no visible evidence of a decisive structural refactor of a shared cause that flips many downstream assertions at once (level 8+), nor of blind patch-piling on a broken assumption (0-3). Confidence is low because the trajectory file is only an index of step headers with no reasoning prose or observations to confirm the intent behind the edits.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
